about: What a settlement ask can need, and where Steward and Architect stand on each (docs/PLAN.md 'Strange asks'). status: now (built), nearest (an honest nearest version is built today; 'nearest' says what), waits (nothing yet; 'comes' says the plan step or Architect slice). Update a capability's status when the step that brings it ships.

flat_village.name: Architect's flat village (lots, lanes, a square, props)

square_districts.name: districts as squares north, east, south or west of the town

one_style.name: one style for the whole settlement (its style bible)

big_program.name: more buildings than one street holds

zones.name: a settlement in parts, each with its own purpose and style

style_by_part.name: style by quarter or by age (an old town and a new one)
style_by_part.comes: Architect 7c SF (Style format 3: zone Styles related to the settlement Style)

biome_aware.name: knowing the biomes the claim spans

land_placed_districts.name: districts laid along the land (a biome edge, a river, a ridge)

walls_gates.name: walls along a boundary, with gates

sculpted_forms.name: big custom forms (a crater, an island, a sky city)
sculpted_forms.nearest: relief, terraces, rock spires, ice spikes, giant trees and mushrooms; a crater or a floating island not yet

over_water.name: buildings over or on water (stilts, a lagoon)
over_water.nearest: ponds, quays, waterfalls and water gates; buildings stand on dry ground beside the water
over_water.comes: Architect 7b AF/SL (the water affordance, stilt lots)

steep_ground.name: buildings on cliffs, terraces and steep ground

carved_interiors.name: rooms, halls and shafts carved into rock or under ground
carved_interiors.nearest: tunnels through rock and caves by the forms; rooms carved into rock not yet

underwater.name: building under water (domes, a sunken town)
underwater.comes: not planned (connector.tube and form.seabed_site are reserved past 7c)

off_ground.name: building on trees, giant mushrooms or stilts above dry ground
off_ground.comes: Architect 7b SL (layout.elevated: canopy and ledge lots)

aerial_connectors.name: bridges and walkways in the air (rope bridges, sky walks)

other_dimensions.name: settlements in the Nether or the End, or across dimensions
other_dimensions.comes: not planned (flat villages are Overworld only; a stockpile is one dimension)

free_layouts.name: layouts beyond a street: a ring, a spiral, a grid, an organic hamlet

megastructure.name: one giant structure that is the settlement (a castle, an arcology)

moving.name: a settlement that moves (a nomad camp, a ship)

ruin_style.name: ruins and decay as a look (broken, overgrown, half built)
ruin_style.nearest: whole buildings with a weathered style

hard_rules.name: hard rules over every building (one block type, no right angles, upside down)
hard_rules.nearest: one palette over the settlement (rule.palette); shape, variety and height rules are hints

variety_control.name: control over variety (no two alike, or identical rows)
variety_control.nearest: copies of like buildings, chosen by Steward

growth_arc.name: a planned growth arc (a camp that becomes a city)
growth_arc.nearest: the steward grows the town street by street and proposes districts as it fills

timed_changes.name: changes on a timetable (festival decorations, seasons)

working_modules.name: working farms, mines, rails and channels
working_modules.nearest: irrigated farms and farm ponds, channels and ditches; no mines or rails

inhabitants.name: inhabitants and animals that fit the story

relations.name: relations inside or between settlements (feuds, factions, war)

build_around.name: building around the player's own things (their house, a tree)

refreshed: 2026-11-12: statuses from Architect's plan catalogue (main bdd1fdc0) and what Steward ships (growth through revisions, plan v1 zones, walls and gatehouses, Supplied builds), for Architect's 7c ordering (S-7c-9)
